key_insight: Agrivoltaic solar arrays can meet flexible interconnection export limits by changing panel tilt, turning curtailment into a way to preserve energy production while also benefiting crops.
engineering_relevance: This shows that operational control of tracker angle, not just inverter clipping, can help distributed PV projects comply with grid constraints without sacrificing agricultural co-use.
method: Formulate a seasonal optimization for single-axis tracking tilt.
Maximize PV energy output subject to a real-power export cap.
Use the resulting operating schedule to assess both PV production and crop outcomes.
evidence_signal: A case study over a growing season evaluated the optimized schedules and found agrivoltaic systems can remain within export limits while improving crop yield.
watch_item: Results are case-study specific, so real-world value will depend on site conditions, crop type, tracker hardware, and the exact interconnection limit.
paper_title: Productive Curtailment in Agrivoltaic Systems under Flexible Interconnection Agreements
